newsitem.title: POLAND: Walesa's son sentenced for drink driving.
newsitem.headline: Walesa's son sentenced for drink driving.

text.p: The son of Poland's former president Lech Walesa was given a two-year suspended jail sentence on Monday for a hit-and-run accident while under the influence of alcohol, PAP news agency said.
Slawomir Walesa, one of eight children of the former Solidarity trade-union leader, was also fined 5,000 zlotys ($1,750) and banned from driving for six years.
Driving a borrowed car, Slawomir rammed into the back of a standing vehicle in Warsdaw in 1995, injuring its driver, and then tried to leave the scene.
Now in his 20s, he was under a driving ban at the time for a similar 1992 offence in his hometown of Gdansk, for which he also received a suspended two-year jail term.
"I had expected a stiffer sentence," PAP quoted him as saying as he emerged from the courtroom.
The three eldest Walesa sons have caused their parents numerous headaches, including out-of-wedlock pregnancies, alcohol abuse and reckless driving.
Their mother, Danuta Walesa, has blamed the problems on the lack of fatherly guidance during her husband's long years of political involvement.
While president of Poland, he visited his family in Gdansk only on weekends.
